title: MTEngineSDL capability vocabulary
description: Validated by mtcaps as its FIRST action, not by CI alone: a malformed vocabulary must fail with the offending key and the rule it broke, before anything else runs.

licence.description: LICENSES.txt is generated from this. 'unknown' is not acceptable -- a legally incomplete SBOM that looks complete is worse than an obviously partial one.

provenance.description: submodule / downloaded tarball / git clone / vendored source / committed prebuilt / system package. The third mode -- committed prebuilt -- is otherwise invisible to the model, and the clean-clone proof would not know it was expected.

commercial_safe.description: Decision 0.2 (2026-08-31): resolve refuses a MT_COMMERCIAL_BUILD=1 build that would enable a dependency with this false. Explicit, never parsed out of the licence prose. Required -- vocab.py enforces it; a row without it would silently sit outside the guard.

flag.description: Optional: the single MT_ENABLE_* flag that gates this dependency, for capabilities that enable several flags (the image-codec bundle). Must be in the owning capability's `enables`. Absent means the capability itself is the gate. The commercial_safe deny-list consults it so a flag forced 0 (libheif outside private builds) never errors.

core.description: Always-on libraries belonging to no capability. Without this section LICENSES.txt would omit SDL3, zlib, ALSA, GTK3, freetype, libuv and the committed prebuilts.

propertyNames.description: A capability key must be a legal shell identifier. bash `source` is the binding constraint and it is stricter than PowerShell's ConvertFrom-StringData or CMake's file(STRINGS): anything else is not an assignment, the shell tries to run the line as a command, and every build-*.sh runs `set -e`, so it is a hard build abort.

short.description: The enum enumerator, DISTINCT from the MT_CAP_ token. Two spellings are needed per capability and confusing them does not compile: the tokens are object-like macros in the same generated header, so `enum class MTCapability { MT_CAP_LLM }` expands to `{ 0 }`.

default.description: Rung 4 of resolution: the engine default for a key the manifest does not list. These are set to today's engine behaviour, so a manifest is a deliberate-choices document rather than an exhaustive one.

implies.description: Downward only. Every target must itself be a capability key -- an implication onto a core concept (audio, i18n, ICC) is an unknown key and exits 2.

enables.description: The MT_ENABLE_* library flags the engine turns on to satisfy this capability. Apps never write these.

app_visible.description: Whether this capability's MT_ENABLE_* flags must reach APP translation units. TWO ways it becomes true, and header dependence alone is the wrong test: the flag appears in a header an app TU includes (the httplib ODR shape), OR an app guards on it directly in its own src/. Populated by grepping all four app trees, never by judgement.

acquisition.description: Per-platform script that acquires and builds this capability's dependencies.

artefacts.description: The archive each platform produces. #3.4's hard error needs the path to test; decision A (stub archives) needs the name to stub.

commercial.description: MT_COMMERCIAL_BUILD's effect on this capability. THREE values, because the tree exhibits all three -- a boolean veto would describe none of the FFmpeg decoder cases correctly.

effect.description: none: unaffected. capability-off: the whole capability is withheld. variant: the capability stays ON and a subset of its libraries or decoders is withheld -- the common case.

symbols.description: Phase 6 asserts BOTH directions. The positive matters: a build that silently linked nothing passes the negative check trivially.
